evidence: Liv. 4.32.10: plēnō gradū, “at full pace” (Lewis & Short)
terms.comment: With an adjective it gives the pace: plēnō gradū, citātō gradū (Liv. 28.14.17), quiētō et placidō gradū (Phaedr.); gradum addere, to quicken one’s pace (Liv. 26.9.5) (Lewis & Short). In the plural it is also the steps of a stair.

terms.gloss: a step, pace; the Roman pace of five feet
evidence: Verg. A. 2.724: sequiturque patrem nōn passibus aequīs (Lewis & Short)
terms.comment: The single stride, and as a measure the double step of five feet: mīlle passūs, a mile (Lewis & Short).

phrases.latin: comes quiētō sequitur et placidō gradū
phrases.english: his companion follows at a quiet, steady pace
and he follows his father, not keeping pace with him

phrases.latin: lentō gradū ambulāte, propter aestum sōlis
phrases.english: walk slowly, because of the heat of the sun
